summary: v1.7 raw nmap XML download feature fully verified. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests pass (endpoint returns 200 + application/xml + Content-Disposition attachment with .xml filename + <?xml body; unknown scan → 404; missing auth → 401/403; cross-user scan → 404; recon/vuln/network all produce results.nmap_xml). Frontend: download-nmap-xml-button appears in Recon, Vulnerabilities, and Network pages after completed 127.0.0.1 fast scan; clicking triggers browser download with filename pentestai-127.0.0.1.xml on all three pages. Button correctly hidden when no scan is selected (verified on fresh user with empty scan history). Regressions: /api/auth/register, /api/auth/login, /api/dashboard/stats, /api/scans, /api/scans/{id}/sarif all pass.
critical_code_review_comments: downloadNmapXml() in all 3 pages is identical (~15 lines) — DRY violation. Extract into a shared hook or util in /app/frontend/src/lib/ (e.g. downloadBlobFile). Low priority.

Content-Disposition filename in backend is `pentestai-scan-{scan_id}.xml`, but frontend saves as `pentestai-{target}.xml` — inconsistent naming. Consider honoring server filename via content-disposition parsing, or align both to include scan_id for traceability.

downloadNmapXml() does not validate response content-type before creating the blob (same class of concern already flagged for LaunchDistroButton in iteration_6). If backend returns JSON error via a different error path, the blob would be saved as .xml with JSON content. Guard with res.headers['content-type']?.includes('application/xml').
results.nmap_xml is stored inline inside the scan document in MongoDB — for large network sweeps this can bloat the doc past 16MB BSON limit. Consider GridFS or S3 offload for scans with >1000 hosts.
